channel.title: n8n release notes: editor and nodes
channel.description: Feature-level updates from n8n releases: what shipped in the editor and the integration nodes.

item.title: Open a resource from the Assistant header when no tabs are open
item.description: In the Assistant thread view, when no preview tabs are open, the header now shows a button to open a workflow, data table, or agent directly from a resource picker, instead of a disabled toggle. Selecting a resource opens it in a new tab and shows the preview. Once tabs are open, the header reverts to the usual preview toggle. This applies to both the main Assistant view and the Assistant agent view.

item.title: n8n Node: Add user get operation
item.description: The n8n node now supports a User resource with a Get operation, letting workflows look up a user by ID or email via the n8n public API. An optional 'Include Role' toggle adds the user's global role to the output. This requires instance owner credentials with the user:read API scope, and returns a clear 'User not found' error for unknown IDs or emails.

item.title: Venafi TLS Protect Cloud Trigger Node: Add webhook signature verification
item.description: The Venafi TLS Protect Cloud Trigger now verifies incoming webhook signatures. When the node creates its connector, it generates a secret and checks each delivery's VaaS-Signature header against it, rejecting unsigned or mismatched requests with a 401. Previously any POST to the webhook URL was accepted. Connectors created before this update are unaffected until the workflow is republished. Also fixed a bug where checking for existing connectors could incorrectly error out instead of properly matching and cleaning up duplicates by name.

item.title: Microsoft Agent 365 Node: Send spans to Microsoft through the OpenTelemetry setup
item.description: The Microsoft Agent 365 node now reliably sends conversation spans to Microsoft's Agent 365 observability service through n8n's own OpenTelemetry setup. Previously this only worked on self-hosted instances without Sentry and with n8n's tracing off; it now also works on n8n Cloud and alongside Sentry or n8n OTel tracing. Export remains on by default and can be disabled via ENABLE_OBSERVABILITY=false or ENABLE_A365_OBSERVABILITY_EXPORTER=false; an opt-in env var also forwards these spans to the customer's own OTel endpoint.

item.title: Postgres Node: Add custom SSL certificate support
item.description: Postgres credentials now support custom SSL certificates: a CA certificate, client certificate, and client private key, shown when SSL mode is set to Allow or Require. This enables connections to databases requiring custom TLS trust or client authentication. SSH-tunneled connections now correctly verify the database hostname for TLS. Credential testing also gives a clearer error message suggesting adding a CA certificate when trust errors occur and none is set.

item.title: Mailchimp Trigger Node: Add webhook signature verification
item.description: The Mailchimp Trigger node now verifies the X-Mailchimp-Signature header on incoming webhook deliveries, checking both the HMAC signature and timestamp freshness, and rejects invalid requests with a 401 response. This prevents unauthorized requests from triggering workflows. Existing workflows are unaffected until reactivated, since Mailchimp only provides the signing secret when a webhook is created; deactivating and reactivating the workflow enables verification.

item.title: Zendesk Node: Default new nodes to OAuth2 authentication
item.description: New Zendesk and Zendesk Trigger nodes now default to OAuth2 authentication instead of API Token, since Zendesk is retiring API token support. API Token remains available as an option. Existing workflows using API Token are unaffected and keep their current authentication. The Zendesk API credential also now shows a notice recommending migration to OAuth2, with a link to Zendesk's migration guide.

item.title: Add resolution guidance to the migration rule detail page
item.description: The migration report rule detail page now includes a "How to fix" panel below the header, showing recommended resolution steps for the rule. If no recommendations exist, it links to the rule's documentation or, failing that, to the general breaking-changes docs. For migratable rules, it also points users to the Migrate action in the table.

item.title: Show the project of each workflow in the migration report
item.description: The migration report now shows which project each affected workflow belongs to. A new Project column displays team project names, while personal projects show as "Personal". The column supports sorting by this label and truncates long names, making it easier for admins to identify and assign migration work without opening each workflow individually.

item.title: Mark required credential fields
item.description: Required credential fields in the node editor now display a red asterisk next to their label, making it clearer which credentials must be filled in before saving. Optional credentials remain unmarked. This helps users quickly identify mandatory setup steps when configuring nodes.

item.title: Improve Agent testing and documentation access
item.description: The Agent builder now shows an outlined Test agent button next to the Agent title, making it easier to preview and run agents while building. A new help icon beside the Publish button opens a hover card with a link to Agent documentation, helping new users learn Agent concepts. The Test agent control is disabled with guidance when an agent cannot run.

item.title: Chat Node: Allow Respond to Chat in embedded chat mode
item.description: Embedded chat (via the @n8n/chat widget) now supports the "Using Response Nodes" response mode in the Chat Trigger, matching hosted chat. This lets Respond to Chat nodes deliver replies over a websocket even after a workflow pauses and later resumes, such as when an AI Agent calls a sub-workflow that waits on a webhook. Existing workflows are unaffected, as this mode is opt-in.

item.title: Add mention-only Slack replies for agents
item.description: Slack agents can now be set to reply only when @mentioned, added as a new 'Reply only when @mentioned' option in Slack Channel Settings. When enabled, channel messages, thread replies, and group DMs require a mention; one-to-one DMs still respond as before. The option defaults to off. Slack settings also gained reorganized Conversations and Agent permissions sections, and the approval control is now labeled 'Ask before certain actions.'

item.title: Databricks Node: Enable the Lakebase resource and show the Lakebase Chat Memory sub-node
item.description: The Databricks node now exposes a Lakebase resource in its Resource dropdown, offering Get Many, Insert, Update, Insert or Update, Delete and Execute Function operations against Lakebase Postgres tables, including use as AI Agent tools. The Databricks Lakebase Chat Memory sub-node is now visible in the node picker under AI > Memory, enabling multi-turn chat history storage in Lakebase.

item.title: Workable Trigger Node: Add webhook signature verification
item.description: The Workable Trigger node now verifies each incoming webhook's X-Workable-Signature header against an HMAC-SHA256 hash computed with the credential's access token. Requests with a missing or invalid signature are rejected with a 401 and a warning is logged, preventing unauthorized triggering of workflows. If you change the access token, reactivate the workflow so n8n recreates the subscription with the new token.

item.title: Add Environments group for source control API key scopes
item.description: The API key creation modal now groups source control scopes (sourceControl:read, sourceControl:pull, sourceControl:push) under a new "Environments" section instead of "Instance operations", making them easier to find when creating or editing custom API keys. This is purely a UI reorganization; existing stored scopes, authorization behavior, and the public API are unchanged.

item.title: Microsoft Foundry Chat Model Node: Use the Microsoft Foundry logo
item.description: The Microsoft Foundry Chat Model and Microsoft Foundry Embeddings nodes now display the official Microsoft Foundry logo instead of the generic Azure icon, in both the nodes panel and on the canvas, making them easier to recognize and consistent with their product name.

item.title: Update Preview and enterprise readiness tags for n8n Assistant and Chat
item.description: n8n Assistant is no longer marked as Preview across the sidebar, onboarding, and settings. Chat is now labeled Preview in its settings page and sidebar entry. Both the Assistant and Chat settings pages now show a new 'Limited enterprise support' badge with an explanatory tooltip next to the page title, visible to enterprise-plan users.

item.title: Show the model that answered in the log details header
item.description: The logs view detail header now shows "Answered by [model name]" next to the token count when viewing a chat model node, matching the label already shown in the NDV. The label is omitted when no model name is available in the run data. The tooltip text was also updated to clarify that the provider returns the model name.

item.title: Send users to the admin who can lift a type restriction
item.description: When a node or credential type is blocked, n8n now directs users to the correct admin instead of always pointing to an instance admin. Blocks set by a team project, or opt-in types the project hasn't allowed, now point to that project's admins (falling back to instance owners/admins if none exist); all other blocks still go to instance admins. The dialog lists the right people, and the agent chat refusal message reflects project-level blocks.

item.title: n8n Node: Add action to add a user to a project
item.description: The n8n node now includes a Project resource with an Add User operation. Users can specify a project ID, user ID, and role (Admin, Editor, Viewer, or a custom role slug via expression) to add a user to a project directly from a workflow. On success, the node returns { "success": true }. This requires an n8n instance with project-role support and an n8n API credential.

item.title: Group instance settings links under section headings
item.description: Settings pages are now grouped under headings (Personal, People & access, AI, Integrations, Security, Operations, Billing) in both the Settings sidebar and the main sidebar's Settings menu, making pages easier to find. Several links were renamed for clarity, SSO and LDAP now live under a new Authentication page, AI usage controls moved into the Assistant page, and long lists now scroll with pinned Sign out/back links. The Settings menu also gained full keyboard navigation.

item.title: Edit Image Node: Add v2 using napi-rs/canvas
item.description: The Edit Image node now has a v2, rebuilt on @napi-rs/canvas and @napi-rs/image to replace the deprecated GraphicsMagick-based implementation, and is now the default version for new workflows. Most operations keep the same behavior, but blur now uses a single 'blur radius' parameter, image quality settings apply only to JPEG, and the information operation returns data in a new shape. Existing workflows on v1/v1.1 continue to work unchanged.

item.title: Add dialog props, update the layout, and migrate existing dialogs
item.description: Dialogs across n8n now share a consistent layout with a new body component that standardizes spacing, scrolling, and scrollbar placement. Dialogs gained closeOnOverlayClick, closeOnEscape, and stacked props for finer control, improved close-button alignment and focus order, and a unified description style. Many existing modals (settings, credentials, agents, assistant, workflow reviews, and more) were migrated to this updated dialog system for more consistent behavior and appearance.

item.title: Prevent usage of deprecated nodes
item.description: Nodes marked as deprecated are now frozen in the editor: they can no longer be edited, renamed, disabled, duplicated, cut, or pinned, and can only be removed or replaced. Import and paste still work so parameter values can be copied, but resulting deprecated nodes remain frozen and, depending on configuration, may be blocked from saving. Error messages now suggest the specific replacement node when available.

item.title: Redis Vector Store Node: Consume the `FluentRedisVectorStore` in the RedisVectorStore Node
item.description: The Redis Vector Store node has been updated to v1.4, adding support for advanced query filtering using native Redis query syntax and custom metadata schema definitions (tag, text, numeric, geo fields), with automatic schema inference when none is provided. Existing workflows on v1.3 or earlier keep working unchanged with the simple comma-separated filter; an upgrade notice is shown for older versions.

item.title: Filter migration report workflows by project
item.description: The migration report's rule detail page now includes a Project filter alongside existing filters like owner and status. Admins can filter affected workflows by a specific team project, or view all personal-project workflows together, making it easier to see which teams own workflows impacted by an upcoming breaking change.

item.title: Databricks Node: Show the Vector Store, Embeddings and AI Agent nodes in the node picker
item.description: The Databricks Vector Store, Embeddings Databricks, and Databricks AI Agent nodes are no longer hidden and now appear in the node picker and sub-node pickers. The AI Agent node links to its documentation and is now recognized as an AI root node in the editor and workflow SDK, so the Evaluations wizard offers it like other agent nodes. Existing workflows using these nodes are unaffected.

item.title: Azure OpenAI Chat Model Node: Add an optional Project field to the Foundry credentials
item.description: The Microsoft Foundry (API Key) and Microsoft Foundry (Entra ID) credentials now have an optional Project field, shown when Endpoint Type is set to Microsoft Foundry. The Azure OpenAI Chat Model node uses this credential-level project to list deployments when the node's own Project field is left empty, with the node's value still taking precedence when set.

item.title: Show agent personalisation icon in subagent modal
item.description: When selecting a sub-agent in the agent builder's sub-agent selector modal, n8n now shows that agent's personalized avatar (icon and gradient) instead of a generic bot icon, making it easier to visually identify agents when adding them as sub-agents.

item.title: Let admins notify workflow owners in bulk from the migration rule detail
item.description: Admins reviewing a migration rule's affected workflows can now select multiple rows and click "Notify owners" to email all eligible owners in one request, instead of notifying one workflow at a time. The bar shows how many selected workflows lack an owner, notified rows move to "Notified" with a timestamp, and any skipped rows trigger a warning toast with reasons. Requires the breakingChanges:migrate scope and SMTP configured on the instance.

item.title: Show the model that answered in the AI log header
item.description: The AI log view in the node details panel now shows which model actually answered a request, useful when a model router (e.g. Azure AI Foundry) picks a model different from the one configured on the node. An "Answered by [model name]" item appears next to the token count in both the Rendered and JSON tabs, with a tooltip explaining it may differ from the node's configured model. It only shows when the run data includes a model name, such as for streaming chat model runs.

item.title: Publish agent modal and modal for warning about unpublished workflows
item.description: Publishing an agent now shows a confirmation modal titled "Agent published" explaining that further changes require republishing, with a "Don't show again" option. If the agent uses unpublished workflows as tools, a new modal lists them with links to publish each one, and blocks the publish instead of failing silently. The Workflows picker no longer shows "Not published" labels or disabled incompatible rows.

item.title: Update budget panel when agent executes
item.description: The Agent builder's Settings panel now updates its monthly budget usage automatically when an agent turn finishes, instead of only showing the value from when the panel loaded. The spend amount and progress bar refresh in place without a loading flicker, and if a refresh fails, the last known value stays visible rather than showing 'unavailable'.

item.title: Let admins notify workflow owners from the migration rule detail
item.description: Admins reviewing a migration report rule can now notify a workflow's owner by email directly from the affected workflows list, when SMTP is configured and the row has an owner with an email. Clicking "Notify owner" sends the email and marks the row "Notified"; a follow-up click shows as "Remind" and resends it, with a tooltip showing when the owner was last notified. Notified rows still count as needing a fix and can be reopened or marked won't fix.

item.title: Kafka Node: Make version 2 the default for new Kafka nodes and triggers
item.description: New Kafka and Kafka Trigger nodes added from the panel now default to version 2, which runs on librdkafka instead of the unmaintained kafkajs library and supports additional compression codecs (Snappy, LZ4, Zstd). Existing workflows are unaffected and keep running on their previously saved version. Note: version 2 producers emit one output item per input record, and Acks now maps to all in-sync replicas rather than leader-only.

item.title: Text Classifier Node: Add opt-in confidence scores to the output
item.description: The Text Classifier node now has an opt-in 'Include Confidence Scores' option. When enabled, each routed item gets a classification object with its category, the model's confidence score for that category, and a scores map comparing all categories. Off by default, with unchanged output when disabled, so no node version bump was needed.

item.title: Show multiple workflows in the review detail view
item.description: The review detail view in the Inbox now lists each workflow in a review as a collapsible item, showing its name and pinned version. The first workflow opens automatically, only one stays open at a time, and the selection persists when switching between Activity and Changes tabs. Only the open item renders its diff view, improving performance for reviews with multiple workflows.

item.title: Show the policy reason when an agent tool call is refused
item.description: When an instance policy refuses an agent's tool call in the preview chat, the step now shows a lock icon with a tooltip explaining the restriction, plus a callout stating the tool is restricted on this instance with a link to contact the instance admin. Previously refusals looked like generic tool errors. This requires the type availability policies feature; it doesn't yet cover refusals inside workflow tools.

item.title: Show policy-blocked items in the source control pull modal
item.description: The source control pull modal now shows which workflows or credentials a content-import policy will block before you pull. A banner summarizes how many items are blocked, each tab groups blocked items under 'Not pulled · blocked by policy' with a hover badge explaining why, and the Pull button reflects how many items will actually come in. A separate warning appears if a policy check itself fails during preview.

item.title: Don't save MCP connections without user approval
item.description: In the AI Assistant's MCP server setup, connecting a server now requires explicitly clicking "Add connector" before it is saved. Previously, selecting and authorizing a connector saved it immediately, with no way to discard an unwanted connection. This prevents accidental or unintended MCP server connections from being persisted.

item.title: Monday.com Node: Add V2 with full V1 parity as the default
item.description: The Monday.com node now has a V2 version with full parity to V1, covering Board, Board Group, Column, Item, and Update resources with 39 operations. V2 is the default for newly added nodes, uses resource locators for IDs, and fixes a bug where creating a Column failed when Column ID was left blank. Existing workflows keep running on V1 unchanged.

item.title: Show Gemini models by name and list prioritized models first in model pickers
item.description: Gemini model pickers (Google Gemini Chat Model node, Google Gemini node, and the Agents model picker) now show models by readable product name, like "Gemini 2.5 Pro", instead of raw IDs such as models/gemini-2.5-pro. Models can also be prioritized to appear first in the list. Saved workflow values still use the model ID, so existing workflows are unaffected.

item.title: Replace Windsurf with Devin in the MCP client dialog
item.description: The instance-level MCP "Connect a client" dialog now offers Devin instead of Windsurf (renamed Devin Desktop by Cognition), with an updated official icon and correct position in the IDE group. Selecting Devin shows the shared config file path (~/.config/devin/mcp_config.json) and a copyable mcpServers entry using HTTP transport, matching both the Devin CLI and desktop app configuration formats. No one-click setup button is available for Devin.

item.title: Add Antigravity to the MCP client connection dialog
item.description: The MCP client connection dialog now includes Antigravity in the IDE group, with its own color icon shown in the dropdown and selected-client button. Selecting it displays a copyable mcpServers config snippet with the instance server URL, plus setup steps pointing to ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json, noting that the Antigravity IDE, desktop app, and agy CLI share this file. Gemini CLI remains unchanged in the CLI group.

item.title: Show who created each preference on the Preferences page
item.description: The Preferences page in Settings > Context now shows a 'Created by' column instead of 'Source'. It displays the name of the user who created each preference, with the origin noted in parentheses for preferences added via the n8n assistant or MCP (e.g. 'Jane Doe (MCP)'). If the user no longer exists, only the origin is shown. The MCP label was also renamed from 'Connected AI tool' to 'MCP'.

item.title: Add project selection to Vertex AI credentials
item.description: Google Vertex AI credentials now let you pick a Google Cloud project from a dropdown populated via your service account, or select Custom to enter a Project ID manually. Manual entry remains available while the list loads or if lookup fails. The credential's connection test now checks whichever project (selected or custom) the node will actually use for requests.

item.title: Add Google Vertex AI credentials
item.description: Added a new Google Vertex AI credential type with a Project ID field, usable alongside existing Google Service Account credentials in the Vertex AI Chat Model and Embeddings nodes. Selecting it uses the credential's project for requests, while a node-level Region setting still overrides the credential's Region. The credential includes a connection test that verifies project access via the Vertex AI locations endpoint.

item.title: Recommend Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 models in AI Assistant setup
item.description: The AI Assistant setup model picker now suggests newer models by default: Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 for Anthropic, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra for OpenAI, and updated equivalents for OpenRouter, with the first option in each provider marked as Recommended. Existing instances keep their previously saved model, and the default instance AI model environment variable is unchanged.

item.title: Disable restricted model providers in the agent model selector
item.description: The agent model picker now respects instance or project policies that restrict credential types. Providers blocked by such a policy appear disabled with a lock icon and a note on which scope restricts them; a provider with multiple credential types is only disabled once all its credential types are blocked. If an agent already uses a now-restricted provider, the picker shows a "Restricted" badge instead of the connected marker.
